title: ASEAN leaders, 8 dialogue partners commit to UNCLOS

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and eight dialogue-partners adopted last night a joint declaration of their strong commitment to international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

In their declaration – adopted during the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) in Manila – the ASEAN and its eight dialogue-partners reaffirmed their “shared commitment to maintaining and prompting peace, security and stability in the region, as well as to the peaceful resolution of disputes, without resorting to the threat or use of force, in accordance with international law.”
They called the UNCLOS the indispensable foundation of a more peaceful and prosperous world and freedom of navigation and overflight.
ASEAN’s eight dialogue partners are China, Australia, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia and the United States.

The joint declaration was issued against a backdrop of China’s continued assertion of its expansive claim in the West Philippine Sea, and the hostile activities of its coast guard and navy against local fishermen and civilian vessels.
In their joint declaration, ASEAN and EAS leaders vowed to promote and uphold international law to ensure peaceful settlement of disputes.

They expressed commitment to advancing regional cooperation and promoting the sustainable use and management of marine resources as well as the protection of submarine cables, pipelines and other critical underwater infrastructure.
They also underscored the need for strong political will and international cooperation to affectively address online scams and strengthen the countries’ financial and digital systems.

The leaders expressed grave concern over the escalating threat posed by transnational criminal organizations inflicting harm through online scams, including those originating from scam centers, and associated human trafficking that can have a severe impact on people in vulnerable situations.
The leaders acknowledged the exploitation of digital and other advanced technologies and digital financial platforms by increasingly sophisticated criminal actors.
They also cited the need to strengthen financial and digital systems while acknowledging the severe human consequences associated with scam centers and related criminal activities.
